We investigate the dynamical behavior of two spatially separated atoms within a thermal bath, where their relative positioning allows for the emergence of subradiant states. By employing a quantum trajectory approach, we demonstrate that while initially subradiant populations eventually reach a steady state, the mean photon count in this long-term equilibrium is governed by the average decay time of biexcitonic states. This correlation establishes a direct link between the two-body decay rate and the thermal steady-state occupation. Furthermore, we show that the thermal bath temperature significantly influences the temporal evolution of the quantum correlations between the atoms.

This paper examines the asymptotic stability of a kink featuring internal oscillations within the sine-Gordon (SG) equation, specifically when subjected to a time-dependent perturbation $f(t)$ that vanishes as $t \to \infty$. We demonstrate that if $f(t)$ is an odd function, the Kink's asymptotic stability is preserved. This finding is supported by an energy estimate for the linearized sine-Gordon (LSG) problem, which accounts for the internal oscillations of the kink. The core of this estimate relies on a novel approach to construct a time-dependent Kink approximation.

The Japan Proton Accelerator Research Complex (J-PARC) is set to commence operations in 2021, with its hadron facility poised to become a global leader in high-energy nuclear physics. This facility will enable investigations into nucleon and nuclear modifications of color transparency, a phenomenon where hadrons travel through nuclear matter with significantly reduced interaction cross-sections. The text details the current J-PARC program and outlines future initiatives aimed at exploring color transparency.

Consistency training is an emerging approach designed to enhance the robustness of reinforcement learning agents against distribution shifts. This paper introduces Consistency Training with Virtual Opponent Discrete Perturbation (CVDDP), a novel method that enforces consistency by evaluating the agent's policy against a simulated opponent. The Virtual Opponent is modeled as a Markov Decision Process with a fixed policy, where the agent undergoes training using a specific discrete perturbation. This approach is versatile and can be applied to various existing consistency training techniques. Experimental results demonstrate that CVDDP significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art consistency methods across diverse environments, including those with continuous action spaces.

Endoscopy is a minimally invasive procedure widely used for diagnosing and treating various gastrointestinal disorders. A critical component of this process is identifying polyps, which are often precancerous lesions that can lead to colorectal cancer if left untreated. While deep learning has shown great promise in endoscopic polyp detection, current methods typically rely on processing video frames independently, neglecting the temporal dependencies inherent in the video stream. To address this, we introduce a novel spatio-temporal feature transformation (STFT) module designed to enhance the temporal aspect of the network. This module effectively captures the spatial information of spatio-temporal features and maps them to the subsequent frame, thereby amplifying the representation power of the network. Additionally, we developed a multi-frame cooperation (MFC) module that integrates features from multiple frames to further boost the network's detection accuracy. Extensive experiments on the Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. The source code for this project is accessible at: https://github.com/chenyuan1999/STFNet.

Conventional unequal chance sampling methods necessitate maintaining a comprehensive database of the entire population, a requirement that is often impractical for stream environments due to their vast size and dynamic nature. To address this, this study introduces an unequal chance sampling protocol tailored for streams that functions without a full population database and updates selection probabilities incrementally. The proposed approach ensures that sampled units maintain a positive correlation with their attributes, thereby enhancing representativeness. The efficacy of this new sampling method was demonstrated through a numerical experiment and validated using two real-world stream datasets.

The $rp$-process, which occurs in the most helium-rich regions of the most massive, hot, and rapidly rotating thermonuclear (Type I) X-ray bursts, is characterized by a series of bottlenecks caused by slow nuclear reactions. These delays can cause the process to pause, potentially leading to observable light curves with multiple peaks. We have identified a new bottleneck at the $^{57}$Zn nucleus, which is bypassed via proton emission. This conclusion is drawn from measurements of $^{57}$Zn's $\beta$-delayed proton branching ratio, which was determined to be $(1.0 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-3}$ using the ISOLDE facility at CERN.

This paper examines an analogue of the Manin-Mumford theorem within the realm of algebraic pencils. Specifically, we prove that given a projective variety $X$ defined over a number field $k$ and a rational map $f: X \dashrightarrow \mathbb{P}^1_k$ of degree $d$, the set of $k$-rational points on $X$ that map to infinite-order points under $f$ resides in a finite union of subvarieties of $\mathbb{P}^1 \times X$ sharing a specific geometric characteristic. Additionally, we demonstrate that if $X$ is of general type, then for sufficiently large $d$, these rational points are contained in a finite union of divisors belonging to a particular linear system.

This study presents an analysis of Very High Energy (VHE) gamma-ray emission from 16 selected pulsars located in the Northern Hemisphere, utilizing data from the VERITAS telescope array. The sample was selected based on their high spin-down luminosity, a key indicator of potential VHE emission. The observations span a 12-year period, with the majority of the pulsars being monitored for at least 10 years. The data underwent standard VERITAS analysis procedures, including the removal of background events and the application of a likelihood-based search for point sources. No significant emission was detected in the vicinity of any of the observed pulsars; consequently, upper limits were established on the VHE flux for each target.

This study examines reaction-diffusion equations featuring nonlocal boundary conditions on uneven domains. We demonstrate that the long-term dynamics of the system are governed by an extended reaction-diffusion model that incorporates the singularities arising from domain shape irregularities.

Ultra-Compact Dwarfs (UCDs) are massive, dense stellar systems that bridge the gap between globular clusters and dwarf galaxies. While their origins remain uncertain, they are believed to be either stripped cores of globular clusters or tidally disrupted dwarf galaxies. This study introduces a machine learning approach to identify extragalactic UCDs, utilizing a dataset of 1,000 objects from the SDSS DR14 catalog. The method employs a Random Forest classifier to distinguish UCDs from other extragalactic sources based on photometric and morphological features. To ensure the reliability of the classification, we apply an explainable AI technique using SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) to determine which features most significantly drive the results. The model achieves an accuracy of 90.1%, with precision and recall of 90.1% and 90.1% respectively. Furthermore, the SHAP analysis reveals that the most critical distinguishing factors are the object's apparent magnitude, isophotal radius, and color.

Simulations are a potent instrument for investigating intricate systems, offering a cost-effective method to evaluate and contrast diverse strategies. Although their application is widespread in recommendation systems, a systematic examination reveals a scarcity of research specifically addressing simulation methodologies for this domain. This paper introduces a framework designed to guide the development of simulations for recommendation systems. We illustrate the utility of this framework through a case study involving the optimization of an online retail recommendation engine. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and potential hurdles associated with implementing simulations in such contexts.

This study examines the hypothesis testing of a truncated sample average when data follow an exponentially decaying distribution. It establishes that the large deviation probability for the truncated estimator adheres to the steepest descent principle. Furthermore, the Stein's method is utilized to demonstrate asymptotic normality regarding the truncated estimator's cumulative distribution function. Finally, the optimal large deviation rate function for the corresponding loss function is derived through the lens of Sanov's theorem.

This study introduces a novel approach to motor visualization classification using EEG signals, which integrates a specialized convolutional neural network (CNN) with a database of 1,000 samples from 10 subjects. The architecture employs a multi-scale convolutional filter bank derived from a sinc function, alongside a recurrent neural network (RNN) designed to capture temporal dependencies. Experimental results demonstrate that this hybrid model outperforms traditional methods relying on bandpower extraction and spectral-spatial features. Specifically, the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 78.4% and a Cohen's Kappa score of 0.56, with an average classification latency of 1.2 seconds.

We examine the link between the noncommutative $AdS_2$ space and its corresponding anti-de Sitter conformal algebra, specifically utilizing the relation principle. This approach enables the derivation of the non-Spinor field action, which is subsequently compared with the results obtained from the oscillator method.

The study addresses the challenge of matching kidneys from deceased donors to recipients, aiming to maximize transplants involving ideally incompatible organs. It introduces a novel framework that integrates both medical constraints and patient/ donor preferences. This approach utilizes a binary variable for each potential transplant pair to indicate acceptance, governed by a predefined set of constraints. The objective is to maximize the count of approved transplants. Additionally, two distinct preference models are examined: one where donors and recipients act as single entities with unified desires, and another treating them as independent agents with separate preferences. These models are applied to real-world data from the Italian kidney registry. Results indicate that adopting the independent-agent preference model leads to a greater number of accepted transplants compared to a model based on joint preferences.

This study introduces a hybrid HMM-LSTM model designed to enhance the performance of both LSTM and HMM architectures. The proposed model leverages the strengths of each component: it utilizes an LSTM to process input data and generate a sequence of hidden states, which subsequently serve as the input for an HMM to produce the final output. Experimental results indicate that this hybrid model achieves superior performance compared to standalone LSTM and HMM models, as well as other existing hybrid approaches.

This paper investigates the boundedness and compactness properties of generalized integral operators mapping from weighted Bergman spaces to Hilbert spaces. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for these operators to be bounded and compact by employing the reproducing kernel method.

Qualtrits, a global online survey platform, leverages cross-lingual multi-job models to efficiently process millions of multilingual surveys annually. This paper details our strategies for shrinking model size and computational load through weight quantization and knowledge distillation. We evaluate these techniques on two distinct models: one handling 11 languages and another covering 22 languages. Our outcomes demonstrate that applying 8-bit quantization reduces the 11-language model's footprint by 75% and the 22-language model by 70%, while executing inference on CPU at speeds of 1,000 and 2,000 surveys per second, respectively. Furthermore, knowledge distillation achieves an additional 25% reduction in size for the 11-language model with minimal accuracy loss. Collectively, these advancements have cut our annual cloud expenses by 60% and accelerated survey turnaround times by 30%.

In this article, drawn from a keynote speech delivered at the 2022 IEEE Data Driven Computing Symposium, I outline a personal perspective on the timing, location, and methods of data sharing within machine learning. I examine the risks and opportunities associated with data sharing, emphasizing the critical need for robust privacy protections. The discussion highlights the transformative potential of open data sharing for advancing machine learning research and outlines a framework for establishing data sharing standards that are both secure and effective.

This research investigates the geometric and arithmetic properties of decomposed richelot mappings $\phi: J(C) \rightarrow J(C')$, where these structures arise from hyperelliptic curves $C$ and their quotients $C'$. We establish that the image varieties of such mappings are not necessarily complete intersections. Furthermore, the study derives explicit formulas for the induced polarization and the genus of the quotient curve $C'$. Additionally, the concept of decomposed richelot mappings is extended to handle cases involving multiple covers.

We report the discovery of three magnetic hot subdwarf B (sdB) stars, designated SDSS J002252.3+414008, SDSS J002252.3+414008, and SDSS J002252.3+414008, which exhibit magnetic fields ranging from 1000 to 10000 Gauss. These stars were identified through the SDSS Stripe 82 survey and confirmed via spectroscopy using the SDSS 2.5m telescope. Their discovery is significant because sdB stars are typically non-magnetic, and their magnetic fields are likely generated via differential rotation during the merger of two non-magnetic progenitors. We analyzed the stars' properties, including their effective temperatures, surface gravities, and chemical abundances, and compared them to non-magnetic sdB stars. Our results indicate that the magnetic sdB stars share similar characteristics with non-magnetic ones, suggesting they formed through a comparable process. Additionally, we investigated the relationship between magnetic field strength and surface gravity, finding no correlation. However, we did observe a trend where magnetic field strength correlates with the abundance of helium and heavier elements, implying that magnetic sdB stars may have experienced more extensive mixing than non-magnetic ones.

We address the challenge of estimating a $p \times p$ symmetric, positive semi-definite matrix with rank $r$ drawn from a Gaussian scale mixture model, where observations consist of independent vectors $X_i \sim N_p(\mu, \Sigma)$. We introduce a novel estimator, LowRankGSR, which combines Gaussian reduction with volume selection. This approach first projects the data onto the principal components of the sample covariance matrix to obtain one-dimensional projections, then estimates both the underlying rank $r$ and the matrix $\Sigma$ by identifying the $r$ directions that maximize the product of the lengths of these projections. We establish that LowRankGSR is consistent for estimating $\Sigma$ and the rank $r$ under mild conditions. Furthermore, we derive a minimax lower bound for the risk associated with estimating $\Sigma$ and compare it against the risk of LowRankGSR. Finally, we validate the estimator's performance through a simulation study.

Wikipedia represents the largest multilingual encyclopedia available on the internet, with the English version alone hosting over 5.6 million articles. These pages are maintained through a collaborative process where users can add, modify, or delete content. Every alteration is recorded in a revision history log that details changes to the article body, edit summaries, edit dates, contributor identifiers, and editor IP addresses. Although this metadata is crucial for analyzing the platform, researchers often face difficulties accessing it because the logs are stored in an obscure, non-standardized format. To address this limitation, we introduce WikiHist.html, a freely accessible repository containing comprehensive revision history data for the entire English Wikipedia. This resource offers a standardized, machine-readable HTML structure designed to facilitate efficient data extraction and analysis.

We examine a bilayer system of two quantum Hall layers, twisted relative to one another, and separated by a small distance. The system is subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field and a lateral electric field. We demonstrate that this configuration supports a stable, uniform magnetization characterized by a meron-antimeron lattice. The resulting magnetic texture features a lattice of merons and antimerons, where each carries an effective charge of $e$. The arrangement of these meron-antimeron pairs forms a square grid, with the orientation of the meron and antimeron sides aligned parallel to the layers' respective Fermi surfaces. The spacing between opposite charges is determined by the interplay of the external magnetic and electric fields, as well as the twist angle. We further explore the characteristics of the meron-antimeron interface, which hosts a domain wall with a specific spin polarization.

This study explores the concept of extrinsic flatness, formalizing the geometry of an observer possessing two distinct metric definitions: one describing their local physical reality and another representing an external, non-flat background. By employing the framework of null geometry, we establish a coordinate-independent approach to analyze relationships between these coexisting spaces. We demonstrate that this methodology offers a robust and precise means of characterizing the interaction between these spatial frameworks.

We introduce a novel method to direct colloidal particles within nematic liquid crystals (NLC) by utilizing a rigid, unpatterned substrate. This surface induces a specific type of nematic distortion known as nematic n-anchoring. The resulting NLC configuration creates a "tunable" environment where the colloid particles are guided along the desired path. This approach is based on the principle of colloidal particles aligning with the liquid crystal molecules along the surface normal. The ability to adjust the colloid pathways is achieved by altering the undulation of the underlying surface. This work demonstrates a new and flexible strategy for manipulating colloidal particles within NLCs.

This study examines how the external sensitivity of a rubble-pile asteroid changes during a distant planetary encounter, specifically focusing on the asteroid's shape. We employ a discrete element method (DEM) to simulate the asteroid's response to tidal forces, comparing outcomes from spherical and elongated asteroid models. Our findings indicate that the asteroid's shape significantly influences its internal structural response to these forces. Specifically, the maximum tidal stress occurs within the exterior region of the asteroid, where the local stress-to-asteroid-strength ratio is highest. Consequently, the probability of asteroid disruption during such encounters is markedly greater for elongated shapes compared to spherical ones.

We introduce a quantum algorithm designed to sample rare conformational shifts within biomolecules. This approach employs an adaptive strategy to mitigate the high cost of quantum Hamiltonian simulation, while utilizing techniques from quantum machine learning to forecast molecular configurations. The algorithm's efficacy is demonstrated through the modeling of a peptide's dynamics.

Polarization measurements of the inverse-Compton scattered light from relativistic jets offer a unique probe of the electron energy distribution and the polarization state of the scattering target photons. This study introduces MAPPIES, a Monte-Carlo simulation designed to model the spectral and polarization characteristics of inverse-Compton radiation. The code incorporates the effects of relativistic beaming, Doppler boosting, and the influence of the observer's line of sight on the resulting spectra. We present the results of the simulations for various jet geometries and compare them with data from the Swift and Chandra observatories. Furthermore, we provide an overview of the code's architecture and its capabilities for modeling complex jet environments.

The Arctic Ocean's sea ice is characterized by a highly heterogeneous structure, featuring a mix of thin and thick floes alongside areas of open water. This variability is influenced by numerous factors, including oceanic and atmospheric conditions, as well as the physical properties of the ice itself. This study utilizes a simple model to simulate the seasonal evolution of the Arctic ice thickness distribution, focusing on the roles of atmospheric heat fluxes, the initial ice thickness, and the size of the Arctic basin. The results indicate that the timing of the maximum annual sea ice thickness is primarily determined by the atmospheric heat flux and the size of the Arctic basin, whereas the timing of the minimum thickness relies mainly on the initial conditions and the heat flux. Furthermore, the research highlights that the Atlantic Ocean's contribution to the Arctic sea ice budget is critical, as it significantly affects the seasonal cycle of ice thickness.

This paper introduces the notion of the Weierstrass semigroup at multiple points on nonsingular curves and, utilizing this framework, derives the semigroups for certain maximal curves. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these structures cannot be subsumed within the semigroups derived from the Hermitian curve.

Deep learning has significantly advanced Singing Voice Generation (SVG), enabling the creation of high-quality audio where a singer performs a target melody at a chosen speed. This paper examines the evolution of SVG from early methods to contemporary deep learning architectures. It details the underlying mechanisms of these systems, including singing voice separation, lyric and score transcription, and synthesis. Furthermore, the study explores practical applications of SVG within the music industry and outlines future research directions.

Birdsong datasets are essential for training and assessing machine learning models designed to analyze birdsong. This paper introduces the NIPS4Bplus dataset, an updated version of the NIPS4B collection that expands the available birdsong recordings from 10 species to 17. The new dataset comprises 1,000 recordings per species, totaling 12,000 files, with a focus on high-quality, precisely labeled data. This update significantly increases the number of available recordings for six of the original species and adds seven entirely new species. The dataset is accessible via https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4410202.

Event cameras are emerging as a promising alternative to traditional frame-based sensors, offering superior temporal resolution and low latency. However, their raw outputs are unsuitable for direct use in standard computer vision frameworks. This paper introduces a method to calibrate event cameras, converting their raw data into frame-based outputs compatible with conventional pipelines. We evaluate this approach using two datasets: one featuring a standard RGB camera and another using a commercial event camera. Our results demonstrate that the proposed calibration effectively supports diverse vision tasks, including optical flow estimation and object detection.

Graphs serve as a versatile data structure capable of representing diverse real-world scenarios, including social networks, knowledge graphs, and molecular structures. Consequently, numerous machine learning algorithms have been developed to address various tasks within graph-structured information. This work offers a comprehensive survey of graph-based deep learning methods, examining their underlying architectures, key contributions, and applications. We categorize these approaches into three primary types: graph convolutional networks, recurrent graph neural networks, and graph transformers. Furthermore, this study outlines promising future directions for research in graph understanding.

We present a full classification of $\Sigma_{2}$-extraordinary collections, with applications demonstrating that every $3$-dimensional linear space can originate as the cohomology of a $\Sigma_{2}$-extraordinary collection, defined over an arbitrary field.

This study introduces a 3D direction tool designed for retinal surgeries, specifically addressing the challenge of determining the direction of the vitreous cutter. The system utilizes an overhead camera to track a small, highly reflective marker (beacon) affixed to the cutter. By applying a triangulation method, the proposed approach estimates the cutter's 3D orientation. The methodology was validated through both simulations and real-world experiments, demonstrating a 3D direction estimation accuracy of 1.0° ± 0.8° in both simulated and actual retinal surgical environments.
This paper establishes two formulas for the $F$-polynomial associated with Coxeter elements in finite, Weyl groups, and showcases several practical applications.

This paper investigates the viability of the passwordless verification standard FIDO2. It examines the technical and organizational factors that make FIDO2 a viable alternative to traditional passwords, focusing on how it addresses security and usability. The analysis covers the underlying technologies, implementation strategies, and the roles of relevant stakeholders. The findings suggest that FIDO2 offers superior security and convenience compared to passwords, though its adoption faces hurdles including technical complexities, organizational challenges, and user education. The paper concludes with a summary of FIDO2's potential and challenges.

This paper examines the Weyl-Wigner quantization approach applied to the Ising model. It highlights the surprising finding that the classical limit of the Ising Hamiltonian corresponds to the XY model. Furthermore, the study analyzes the behavior of the model under the approach to the continuum and demonstrates that a naive continuum limit results in the vanishing of the associated Weyl-Wigner algebra.

This study examines the impact of YouTube's interface design on user agency. We conducted a user study with 100 participants, presenting them with three distinct YouTube layouts: a desktop version, a mobile version, and an aggregated feed containing both video types. Participants were asked to complete a series of tasks within these interfaces. Our findings indicate that the aggregation of the feed resulted in users performing more actions than the isolated desktop or mobile versions. Furthermore, we discovered that the amount of time users spent on the aggregation interface was greater than on the separate desktop or mobile versions, and this increased duration correlated with the number of actions taken. These results suggest that mixing video sources empowers users to execute more interactions, thereby enhancing their perceived control.

This study demonstrates that the asynchronous $\pi$-calculus possesses functional completeness, provided the underlying set of names is equipped with a standard structure. This result indicates that any function definable within the $\pi$-calculus can be realized by the calculus. The proof relies on constructing the specific canonical encoding, a process that is notably more complex than the one proposed by Betti and Betti. Furthermore, we establish that the calculus is functionally complete when restricted limit the scope of computable functions to those with finite orbits.

This paper introduces a method to generate a compacted gray code based on the lexicographical ordering of labeled trees, designed to significantly minimize signal switching during computer-to-computer communication.

The sPHENIX experiment, situated at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) at Brookhaven National Laboratory, is designed to investigate the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and the properties of hadronization within the context of jet formation. To achieve these goals, the experiment relies on a dual detector setup: a central tracker for inner tracking and a forward calorimetric system for jet analysis. This study details the implementation of the Advanced Calorimetric Topological Tracking System (ACT) on the sPHENIX central tracker to reconstruct particle tracks. The ACT's silicon sensors are arranged in two layers, with the inner layer positioned at a radius of 1.5 cm and the outer at 3.0 cm from the interaction point. The reconstruction process involves identifying and fitting clusters of hits to determine the trajectory of charged particles. The paper outlines the specific algorithms used for cluster finding and fitting, alongside an evaluation of the reconstructed tracks' resolution and tracking efficiency.

This paper examines the numerical solution of stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) employing a stochastic finite element method (FEM) in spacetime. The approach utilizes random temporal interpolation based on Karhunen-Loève (KL) expansion to discretize random variables in time, while standard FEM discretizes them in space. A key contribution of this work is the derivation of a closed-form expression for the jump-term arising from random integration by parts across the stochastic SPDE. This closed-form solution is essential for implementing the method in computational frameworks. The study further demonstrates that the proposed random temporal FEM discretization yields convergence rates of $O(\Delta t^{3/2})$ in time and $O(h^{s+1/2})$ in space, where $s$ represents the polynomial degree of the FEM. These findings are substantiated through numerical experiments.

This paper examines circular flows within signed networks, specifically investigating how to determine the minimum integer $k$ such that the $k$-fold sum of the signed graph $G$ admits an orientation supporting a circular flow where every vertex achieves a current of magnitude 1. We refer to such a structure as a "flow of strength 1." Our primary focus is on establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for a signed graph to possess this property in its $k$-power. Additionally, we demonstrate that circular flows in directed signed networks are mathematically equivalent to the notion of balanced factorizations found in undirected signed networks.

This paper addresses the well-known Modular Subset Total (MST) problem, defined as follows: given a set $S$ of integers and a modulus $m$, identify a subset $S' \subseteq S$ such that the sum of its elements is congruent to $0 \pmod m$. The problem is proven to be NP-hard for $m \geq 3$. While the fastest exact algorithm currently known runs in $O(2^{|S|/2})$ time, this efficiency is achieved only through randomized methods. The authors introduce a deterministic algorithm with a runtime of $O(2^{|S|/2-1} + |m|^2)$, which is marginally faster than the randomized baseline. This approach is further optimized to $O(2^{|S|-1} + |m|^3)$ when $|m|^3$ is precomputed. The study also establishes an upper bound of $O(c^{|S|} + |m|^2)$ for some constant $c < 2$, along with an approximation algorithm offering a $|m|^2$-approximation ratio in $O(|S| \cdot m^2)$ time.

Cell migration is a fundamental process in embryogenesis, where cells must navigate complex environments to reach their designated positions. Although the mechanisms governing this movement are well-understood in epithelial and mesenchymal cells, the rules of non-epithelial and non-mesenchymal migration remain obscure. To address this gap, we examined the behavior of hemocytes in *Drosophila melanogaea* embryos. These cells are essential for the embryo's innate immunity, as they must be distributed throughout the embryo to form a protective layer around the serosal cavity. Our findings reveal that hemocyte migration is highly dynamic and characterized by a unique, highly coordinated group behavior. We observed that these cells frequently execute "tango-like" movements, where they approach one another, rotate around a shared center of mass, and then separate. This behavior is driven by a specific interaction between cells that increases attraction at short distances but triggers repulsion at longer ranges. This dynamic movement is further facilitated by the cells' ability to transiently alter their mechanical properties, transitioning between rigid and fluid states. These observations provide novel insights into the physical forces and mechanisms underlying cell migration in non-epithelial and non-mesenchymal tissues.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have become the standard for speech recognition, yet their practical application is often hindered by the scarcity of labeled data. While semi-supervised learning (SSL) offers a solution, it typically demands computationally expensive pre-training of a DNN on vast amounts of unlabeled audio. This paper introduces a novel semi-supervised framework that integrates a Siamese network with a DNN to enhance speech recognition without the need for such expensive pre-training. By training the Siamese network to generate discriminative features from unlabeled audio, the system enables the DNN to achieve superior performance with only a minimal amount of labeled data. The study evaluates this approach on the LibriSpeech 100-hour dataset, demonstrating that the method achieves 28.0% WER using merely 100 hours of labeled data and reaches 20.4% WER when combined with 600 hours of unlabeled audio.

This study details the 2021 updates to the non-elastic axial and vector morphology functions, $F_A$ and $F_V$, utilized in lepton-nucleon scattering analyses. These functions are essential for extracting the nucleon's non-elastic axial and vector form factors from reduced virtual Compton scattering amplitudes. The updates incorporate new experimental data on the nucleon's elastic form factors and account for the influence of meson exchange currents on the scattering amplitudes. The paper also examines the sensitivity of form factor extractions to variations in morphology functions and evaluates the sensitivity of Rosenbluth and $Q^2$-extrapolations to the chosen function set. The authors conclude that the new 2021 functions offer a more consistent description of existing data compared to earlier iterations.

This study addresses the near-certain stabilization of discrete-time adaptive systems characterized by a hidden Markov model within linear-quadratic frameworks. The authors demonstrate that the near-certain stabilizability of the regulated system is equivalent to the near-certain stabilizability of the parameterized system associated with each state of a hidden Markov chain. Furthermore, the paper introduces an LQ optimal regulator featuring a dynamic output feedback mechanism with a finite-dimensional, stable precompensator. This approach guarantees that the closed-loop parameterized system achieves near-certain stability, provided the nominal system is both near-certain stabilizable and the initial compensator's order matches the dimension of the unobserved state vector.

Active inference serves as a leading framework for modeling goal-directed behavior, positing that the brain continuously minimizes free energy by selecting actions that optimize anticipated sensory inputs. This paper extends the active inference paradigm to accommodate multi-modal and multi-dimensional sensory data. We introduce a new approach to defining free energy for such complex inputs, utilizing the concept of branching time to model the inherent multi-dimensional nature of this free energy. We validate our framework through simulations of two-dimensional active inference, demonstrating that the agent can successfully localize its position within a two-dimensional maze.

This study examines the formation of Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) solitons within a frigid quark-gluon plasma. We derive the KdV equation for long-wavelength perturbations in a cold quantum relativistic fluid, accounting for the influence of a constant external magnetic field. Numerical results demonstrate that both the velocity and the full width of these solitons are governed by the fluid's compressibility and viscosity, respectively.

This characterization is derived from the fact that a locally convex space $E$ possesses Eberlein-Giothendieck topology if and only if it can be represented as a subspace of a weak* topology on some Banach space $Y_\alpha$. This result is obtained by applying a series of transformations to $E$, specifically by embedding it into a Banach space $Y_\alpha$ such that $E$ is a subspace of $Y_\alpha^*$. This study examines the isochronous properties of 1-degree-of-freedom systems, specifically focusing on the conditions required for such behavior. We introduce a novel approach to establish these criteria and apply them to various physical and mathematical models. Our analysis reveals that the conditions for zero time variation are equivalent to those for zero parameter sensitivity. Furthermore, we demonstrate that an oscillatory system exhibiting zero total energy must also possess a stable equilibrium point.

This paper introduces a novel technique for generating periodic orbits in the Lorenz system by integrating the method of periodic orbits with the concept of resemblance signature curves. A key advantage of this approach is that it allows researchers to specify the duration of the desired orbit, enabling the creation of periodic solutions of any length.

This paper examines the properties of the Linearized Approximation of the process (LÃ–) for random differential equations (RDEs), where both randomness in coefficients and initial conditions are driven by Lévy processes. We demonstrate that these properties hold for the LÃ– when applied families of distributions of RÃÃ solutions under appropriate regularity conditions. This extends previous findings on LÃÃ properties established for RÃÃ with random initial conditions and deterministic coefficients.

We examine twisted Laplacians on a compact, complex, Riemannian manifold $X$ relative to a holomorphic vector bundle $E$ and a holomorphic line bundle $L$. By analyzing the spectrum of this operator, we derive a novel application of the Kodaira vanishing theorem that yields an explicit description of the range of twisted Laplacians. Furthermore, we provide a direct characterization of the range using the Teichmüller representation of $H^{1}(X, E\otimes L)$, which serves as an alternative to the standard Kodaira-Spencer representation.

We introduce FNetAR, a streamlined autoregressive architecture that merges tokens with the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to achieve high-performance sequence modeling. By utilizing FFT to capture long-range dependencies, FNetAR surpasses autoregressive transformers that rely solely on attention mechanisms. Notably, FNetAR delivers the current state-of-the-art results on all benchmarks, including those for language modeling, image modeling, and DNA sequence analysis. Furthermore, FNetAR is significantly more computationally efficient than standard transformers, offering a substantial reduction in both training and inference costs. This efficiency is achieved by integrating tokens with Fourier features, which drastically decreases the number of parameters and the count of autoregressive operations required.

This study investigates the dynamical evolution of the generalized phantom traveler dark energy (GGPDE) model within the Saez-Ballester gravitational theory. By employing a system of coupled differential equations, we analyze the model's stability and examine its cosmological implications. Our findings indicate that the GGPDE model is consistent with the observed accelerated expansion of the universe. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the model's parameter space encompasses both quintessence and inflationary phases.

This study examines a scenario where numerous users, each utilizing a set of services, rely on Network Functions Virtualization (NFV) to access these services. These services are hosted on Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) servers, which are connected via a Network Function Chaining (NFC) graph. The primary objective is to identify an optimal NFC graph that minimizes the aggregate latency across all servers. We model the user services as strategic players within a mean-field game, where each player selects a specific graph to reduce their own latency. The latency of any single service depends on the routing decisions of all services, which are mediated by the MEC servers. We propose a solution to this game using a combination of reinforcement learning and the concept of a Mean Field Equilibrium (MFE). The findings demonstrate that the proposed algorithm successfully converges to the MFE, yielding a network configuration that significantly lowers latency.

We utilize the renormalization group (RG) to investigate a four-fermion model featuring a stochastic Dirac mass term within a $d$-dimensional spacetime. The analysis reveals that the stochastic mass renders the four-fermion interaction non-renormalizable when $d > 3$. However, in three dimensions ($d = 3$), the model exhibits a non-trivial infrared fixed point, allowing us to compute the critical exponents associated with RG flows. These calculations are performed using the $\epsilon$-expansion for $d = 3 - \epsilon$, yielding a critical exponent $\nu \approx 0.75$ that aligns with results from lattice simulations. Furthermore, we establish that the stochastic mass term does not influence the critical exponent $\nu$ governing the RG flow of the conventional deterministic mass term.

Depression is a pervasive mental health condition that significantly impacts individuals' lives. Despite its negative connotations, individuals with the disorder also experience positive emotions. This paper introduces a dataset comprising joyous moments reported by people living with depression, and outlines a series of experiments designed to investigate these positive aspects within the disorder.

This work examines the isospin breaking sector within Sp(4) gauge theory by employing the gradient flow technique to determine the spectrum of the energy density as a function of temperature. The study utilizes a lattice framework with a temporal extent of $N_t=8$ and varying spatial sizes, specifically $N_s=16, 32,$ and $64$. The results indicate that the isospin breaking phase transition is of the first order, with the transition temperature $T_c$ rising as the spatial volume expands. Furthermore, the study reports a significant difference in the transition temperatures between this Sp(4) theory and SU(4) theory, finding $T_c$ to be approximately 10% lower in the isospin breaking Sp(4) case.

This system is of significant interest because it is a potential candidate for investigating the interplay between quantum spin liquid states and superconductivity. Trust management is essential for the operation of Internet of Things (IoT) networks, yet existing research has largely overlooked its application within intelligent vehicular networks. This paper introduces a theoretical framework for trust management specifically designed to address the inherent uncertainties of intelligent transportation systems. The proposed architecture incorporates a dedicated trust update module that accounts for both the inherent fuzziness of trust values and the fluctuating dynamics of trust evolution. By integrating a fuzzy trust aggregation module, the system enables vehicles to derive comprehensive trust assessments from multiple sources. Furthermore, a trust dissemination component is implemented to facilitate the sharing of these aggregated values among vehicles. Simulation results indicate that the proposed approach effectively manages trust under uncertain conditions, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods.

We introduce an algorithm for approximating functions with a monotone derivative using a monotone cubic spline. This spline connects two boundary points via a series of cubic arcs, where each point of intersection between arcs is defined by local extrema. The method's convergence rate is determined by the maximum gradient magnitude and the arcs' length. Additionally, the paper outlines a strategy for determining the appropriate number of cubic arcs and their specific locations.

This paper investigates Taub-NUT spacetimes within anti-de Sitter space coupled to a scalar field, where we derive exact solutions featuring a small parameter $\epsilon$ that vanishes at the black bounce limit. These solutions are derived using the Newman-Janis algorithm applied to AdS-Taub-Bolt configurations, where the scalar field potential is set to $U(\phi)=\frac{1}{2}e^{-2\phi}$. We derive the exact metric for generic $\epsilon$ and analyze its asymptotic behavior for small $\epsilon$. The resulting metric, which includes a logarithmic term in $\epsilon$ dependent on the radial coordinate, is shown to be asymptotically AdS. We also calculate the Hawking temperature and entropy, demonstrating that the entropy remains independent of $\epsilon$ and matches the AdS-Taub-Bolt value. Finally, we demonstrate that the AdS-Taub-NUT solutions are thermodynamically stable.

Although large sound libraries offer a wealth of resources, they complicate the creation of training datasets for sound-based machine learning tasks. This difficulty arises because annotators must constantly browse the vast taxonomy to identify relevant audio files, a process that is both time-consuming and prone to errors. We introduce a method that streamlines the selection of sound files for dataset assembly. Our approach involves creating a concise, high-level representation of the sound library, which annotators utilize to identify sounds that align with their specific requirements. We evaluated this method by comparing its annotation quality and time efficiency against two alternative methods: one utilizing an audio retrieval system and another employing a sound library browser. Our results indicate that our approach achieves superior annotation quality and is more efficient than the sound retrieval baseline. Furthermore, it matches the performance of the sound retrieval system in terms of quality while requiring less time, and outperforms the traditional sound library browser in both quality and efficiency.

This study introduces a general dynamic mean-field theory applicable to systems where individual components interact through a shared, component-independent field. The approach is demonstrated using two distinct examples: an ecological model and a reaction-based framework. In the ecological scenario, the interaction arises from a shared resource, resulting in a competitive exclusion principle. In the reaction framework, the field represents a chemical mediator, yielding a dynamic set of reactions. In both cases, the theory predicts a phase transition between a stable non-equilibrium state and a regime of stochastic extinction.

In the context of the forest fire model, we investigate the statistical distribution of avalanche sizes within the Cayley tree framework. We demonstrate that this distribution is governed by an asymptotic form of the form $P(s) \sim s^{-\tau}$. This behavior is supported by numerical findings indicating the exponent value $\tau = 0.25$, which aligns with theoretical predictions.

This paper introduces a novel framework designed to capture the relationships between multiple sentences in dialogue contexts. By utilizing a question-answering mechanism, the model identifies whether a specific utterance acknowledges another within the conversation history. This approach offers a comprehensive method for depicting how sentences are interconnected. Furthermore, the work presents a new dataset for dialogue coherence, constructed by generating answers to queries about the relationship between pairs of sentences in context. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method significantly surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques in representing sentence connections within dialogue flows.

The Flawlessly Aligned Layer (PML), a domain-truncation technique, has proven effective for simulating wave propagation in unbounded spaces. This technique has been extensively studied for Maxwell's equations, the scalar wave equation, and the elastic wave equation. This review examines the PML's application to hyperbolic wave propagation, highlighting both its theoretical foundations and practical implementations. The text begins by outlining the governing equations for various wave types, followed by an explanation of the PML methodology. Subsequently, it details the PML-adapted equations for specific wave types, analyzes the associated spectral properties, and discusses key implementation challenges. The review concludes by summarizing the PML's advantages and limitations.

This study investigates the interaction between a laser pulse and a jet of droplets. The laser pulse, generated by a 1064-nm pulsed Nd:YAG laser, was directed at a collimated stream of water droplets. The resulting deformation and fragmentation of the droplets were captured using a high-speed camera. The analysis reveals that the droplets' response to the laser-induced pressure wave depends on their size, with droplets smaller than 100 µm vaporizing and those larger than 200 µm deforming. Furthermore, the laser-jet interaction induces a phase shift in droplet oscillations, causing them to collide with the nozzle tip at irregular intervals. This phenomenon was examined across varying laser energies and stream velocities. Ultimately, the study concludes that the laser-jet interaction can effectively deform droplets and induce fragmentation.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a paradigm where physical devices are interconnected via the Internet to exchange data, forming a network of "things" that communicate with each other. While the primary objective of IoT is to enable seamless communication among these devices, the heavy traffic generated by IoT traffic can severely degrade the performance of the Internet. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a framework that integrates Software-Defined Networking (SDN) with the publish-subscribe model. This approach allows IoT devices to subscribe to specific events and receive updates from subscribers, thereby reducing the volume of transmitted data. The study outlines the proposed framework, detailing its architecture, data subscription process, and the integration of IoT with Internet protocols. Additionally, it examines the deployment of this framework within an OpenFlow environment.

The LkH$\alpha\,330$ system, a young T Tauri star exhibiting strong H$\alpha$ emission, is a prime candidate for studying planet formation. We present new ALMA observations of the disk's CO isotopologue emission ($^{12}$CO, $^{13}$CO, and C$^{18}$O) alongside archival data on dust continuum and polarized scattered light. Our analysis reveals that the disk's gas surface density peaks at approximately 100 au, while the dust continuum emission peaks at roughly 30 au, indicating a significant dust depletion in the outer regions. Polarized light observations confirm a complex dust structure, featuring a prominent gap at 100 au and a secondary one at 160 au. By modeling the dust properties, we determine that tiny grains (r $\le$ 10 $\mu$m) are present in the outer disk but absent in the inner disk, whereas massive grains (r $\ge$ 100 $\mu$m) are found in both locations. We attribute the inner disk's dust depletion to dust growth and the outer disk's depletion to dust settling. Furthermore, we detect a strong correlation between the gas and dust depletion radii, suggesting that dust growth and gas accretion onto the star are synchronized processes. This paper introduces a novel concept of a vector-valued metric defined over the domain of symmetric positive definite matrices. We establish fundamental properties of this metric and introduce the associated vector-valued disk. Furthermore, we define a specific norm called the Lyapunov norm within this domain and demonstrate that the perimeter of every set is invariant under addition of the Lyapunov norm. In addition, we outline a generalized form of the Gyrocalculus, which serves as an analogue to standard calculus within this specific metric framework.

The European Union's 2030 climate strategy necessitates the decarbonization of the energy sector, a transition that will require substantial infrastructure investment. This study examines the economic and environmental viability of a European hydrogen network, specifically contrasting it with current electricity grid models. We analyze the marginal costs of transporting energy via both networks, utilizing a simplified model of European transport to demonstrate that hydrogen offers significant competitive advantages over electricity. Our findings indicate that, under current conditions, hydrogen is cheaper than electricity for long-distance transmission. Furthermore, when integrating a 2050 decarbonization scenario, the economic superiority of a hydrogen grid becomes even more pronounced. Ultimately, this research highlights the substantial environmental and economic benefits of shifting from an electricity to a hydrogen grid.

The Sun's magnetic field is characterized by a significant degree of anisotropy, with a primary component oriented horizontally and parallel to the surface. This anisotropy influences the travel duration of solar energetic particles (SEPs) moving through the heliosphere. Theoretical models indicate that particles traveling along the axis of the horizontal magnetic field experience a shorter journey time than those moving perpendicular to the field. This study utilizes the Parker equation to derive an analytical solution for the differential flux of SEPs, examining how the differential flux ratio (DFR)—defined as the flux parallel to the field divided by the flux perpendicular to it—varies with the field's anisotropy. The DFR is observed to depend on the particle's rigidity, the field's anisotropy, and the direction of motion relative to the field. The analysis reveals that the DFR peaks when particles move parallel to the field and drops to a minimum when they move perpendicular to it. Furthermore, the DFR is inversely proportional to particle rigidity, meaning lower-rigidity particles exhibit a larger DFR. The study concludes that the DFR is a valuable metric for detecting anisotropy in the Sun's magnetic field, as it is sensitive to the field's orientation, particle rigidity, and the specific direction of particle motion.

Squeezed light serves as a vital resource for enhancing the precision of optical quantum metrology. However, achieving this state is difficult because it demands high-efficiency nonlinear optical processes, which are often hard to realize in integrated photonic systems. In this study, we present a topological strategy to protect squeezed light propagation on photonic chips. We demonstrate that by utilizing topologically protected waveguides, we can achieve effective squeezing without relying on low-loss nonlinear elements. Our findings indicate that topological protection offers a viable and promising method for generating and preserving squeezed light on integrated photonic platforms.

This paper introduces a new approach for generating time-optimal trajectories for drones navigating complex environments. While existing methods typically rely on a two-stage process—first creating a trajectory using a simplified model, then refining it with fidelity models—this study proposes a unified framework that directly generates high-fidelity paths. The core methodology involves formulating the trajectory generation problem as a nonlinear optimal control task, which is subsequently transformed into a two-point boundary value problem (TPBVP). To solve this efficiently, we employ a novel fluid time-stepping algorithm that utilizes a specific neural network architecture. This network is trained to predict the solution to the TPBVP, with its weights initialized using outputs from a previous iteration of the time-stepping process. The study demonstrates that this strategy significantly enhances computational speed, enabling the rapid generation of time-optimal paths for drones in intricate settings.

This paper introduces a new algebraic structure for q-linear conjuguecyclic codes defined over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, which are viewed as subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^n$ that remain invariant under the action of the group $G_q(n) = \langle \sigma, \pi \rangle$. This group is generated by the Frobenius automorphism $\sigma$ and the cyclic permutation $\pi$. We establish a one-to-one correspondence between these codes and $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}[x,I_\sigma]$-modules, where $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}[x,I_\sigma]$ denotes the noncommutative twisted polynomial ring. This result extends the findings of Calderinb and Ward, who demonstrated a similar isomorphism for classical conjuguecyclic codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Furthermore, the study derives minimal polynomial representations for the generators of $G_q(n)$ and examines the link between invariant polynomials and invariant subspaces under the group's action. Finally, the paper applies these concepts to the creation of optimal local minimum distance (MLD) codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.

The 2021 Community Involvement Frontier Snowmass report presents findings from the Thematic Group on Career Pipeline and Advancement (Comf2). This group aims to address the underrepresentation of underrepresented groups (URMs) within the particle physics community by identifying specific barriers to their career advancement and proposing actionable solutions. The document serves as a strategic guide for the Frontier Snowmass Working Groups, offering concrete recommendations to support equitable hiring, retention, and advancement practices.

This paper details an analysis of $W$ boson polarization within $t\bar{t}$ events using ATLAS detector data from $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 8$ TeV, focusing on the lepton+jets decay signature. The dataset comprises an integrated luminosity of 20.2 fb$^{-1}$ collected in 2016. The $W$ boson's spin alignment is examined through the angular distribution of its decay products, specifically the $W$'s momentum relative to the quark that produced it. This distribution is modeled using a parameter, $\alpha_W$, which is determined to be $0.09 \pm 0.03$ (stat.) $\pm$ 0.01 (syst.) $\pm$ 0.01 (lumi). This result aligns with the Standard Prediction of $\alpha_W = 0.08$ with a combined uncertainty of 0.01.

This study reexamines the light-cone distribution functions (LCDAs) for $D$-mesons, specifically focusing on the longitudinal component of the twist-2 distribution ($f_1^L$) and the twist-3 distribution ($\tilde{g}_1^L$). By employing the $SU(3)$ flavor symmetry, we establish a connection between the $D$-meson LCDA parameters and those of pions and kaons. Furthermore, we determine the LCDA parameters for $D$-mesons using QCD sum rules, with particular attention to the non-perturbative parameters $\phi_1^L$ and $\phi_2^{(3)}$. Our findings indicate that the pion twist-2 LCDA parameter $\phi_1^L(q^2=0)$ is $0.21 \pm 0.03$ GeV, which aligns with previous results derived from lattice QCD.

The signed graph spectrum of a graph $G$ is defined as the collection of all eigenvalues from every possible signed graph that can be formed using $G$ as its underlying graph structure. Similarly, the spectrum of the power hypergraph $\mathcal{P}(G)$ is the set comprising the eigenvalues from all possible bipartite hypergraphs that can be constructed based on the hyperedges of $\mathcal{P}(G)$. The authors demonstrate that the spectrum of the power hypergraph is actually a proper subset of the signed graph spectrum of the associated graph $G$. Furthermore, they provide a method to identify the exact members of this proper subset.

The collaborative localisation capability of the space-based broadband network operator Starlink (owned by SpaceX) is becoming increasingly significant. This study examines the theoretical performance boundaries for localising Starlink satellites by analysing the broadcast signals used for data transmission. By leveraging the known structure of these signals, the research proposes a new method to estimate satellite position based on the received broadcast content. This approach is benchmarked against a traditional method that relies solely on detecting signal presence to infer location. The study further evaluates the localisation accuracy of both techniques under various network configurations and signal parameters, with results indicating that incorporating broadcast content yields substantial performance gains.

Hot Jupiters are known to experience tidal forces that can synchronize their rotation with their orbital periods, yet this synchronization is not always achieved. For planets with high orbital eccentricities, tidal effects can be particularly pronounced. This study reports transit timing variation (TTV) data for the exoplanet XO-3b, which exhibits a significant deviation from perfect synchronization. By analyzing transit times across multiple observations, we determined that the planet's orbital period is increasing at a rate of $(1.0 \pm 0.2)$ seconds per year. This variation is attributed to tidal interactions between the planet and its host star. The observed TTVs provide strong evidence that the planet is undergoing tidal evolution, with its orbit gradually circularizing. This process is expected to result in a future state where the planet's rotation period matches its orbital period, effectively synchronizing them.

The 21-cm global signal offers a promising avenue for investigating the Universe's history during the Epoch of Reionization. However, the anticipated signal is extremely faint, making it susceptible to contamination from unmodeled astrophysical processes. To address this, we introduce a Bayesian framework designed to estimate and remove such foregrounds. This method utilizes a Bayesian approach to infer the signal and foregrounds by calibrating the input data against a 21-cm simulation, thereby accounting for instrumental effects and noise. We apply this to a 21-cm simulation of the Epoch of Reionization, incorporating a frequency-dependent noise model and a foreground model that includes a disturbance wave component. This calibration process successfully isolates the 21-cm signal while filtering out the foregrounds. We also assess the impact of a Gaussian random field on the foreground power spectrum. Our results indicate that the proposed calibration method effectively recovers the 21-cm signal and suppresses foregrounds, with minimal impact from the Gaussian random field.

This work examines the relationship between the quantum cohomology of the Grassmannian $Gr(k,n)$ and that of its geometric bundle, defined as $P(Gr(k,n)) = BGL(k)^\backslash Gr(k,n)$. We demonstrate that the quantum Chern classes of any bundle over a Fano manifold can be expressed as polynomials in the bundle's quantum tangent bundle Chern classes. Applying this result to the geometric bundle yields a formula for its quantum Chern classes in terms of the quantum Chern classes of the base manifold. Furthermore, we establish a decomposition theorem for the quantum tangent bundle of the bundle, showing that the quantum tangent bundle of the bundle, $T_P P$, is isomorphic to the direct sum of the pullback of the tangent bundle of the base manifold, $p^* T_M$, and the quantum tangent bundle of the bundle restricted to the base, $T_P P|_M$.

This paper introduces an approach for analyzing Alzheimer's disease clinical trials by employing natural cubic splines to model the dose-response relationship. The study demonstrates that this proposed method offers a more precise fit compared to conventional linear models. Furthermore, we examine how the method performs in scenarios involving outliers and assesses the impact of varying the smoothing parameter on the results.

This paper introduces CRAWLING, a crowdsourcing approach designed to automatically identify parking spots using mobile devices. The method leverages readily available sensors, such as GPS and accelerometers, to capture vehicle movement data. This data is then processed to distinguish between driving and stationary states, with the system extracting parking location details only during stationary periods. The study validates the algorithm's efficacy through tests conducted on both real-world and synthetic datasets. The results demonstrate that CRAWLING achieves an accuracy of 90.8% in detecting occupied spots and an F1-score of 84.5% in identifying available ones. The authors conclude that CRAWLING is a robust, effective solution for automating parking space detection.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) are widely used across numerous fields, including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. However, their training process is opaque, and their internal decision-making mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study investigates the behavior of gradient-based optimizers, specifically focusing on the min-max optimization framework. We demonstrate that the behavior of these optimizers is contingent on the initialization of the parameters. Furthermore, we provide a sufficient condition for the convergence of these optimizers in terms of reaching stationary points.

This study introduces a reflective parametric frequency-selective attenuator (RPFSA) designed to mitigate signal interference in radio frequency (RF) communication systems. The device utilizes a superconducting qubit to generate dynamic parametric modulation, which facilitates the attenuation of unwanted RF signals. By employing a theoretical framework, we calculated the theoretical power dissipation and evaluated the performance of the proposed attenuator. The results indicate that this approach achieves power barriers of up to $\mu$W with sub-dB insertion loss, offering a viable pathway for future parametric frequency-selective attenuator development.

This study examines the dynamics of the COVID-19 outbreak in the extreme scenario where individuals never develop acquired immunity. Under these conditions, the infection cycle transitions continuously between individuals who are susceptible, infected, and recovered. We propose a novel SEIRS model that incorporates the time-dependent probability of an individual being in any of these three states. Our analysis demonstrates that this probability is governed by the basic reproduction number ($R_0$) and the average infectious period ($\tau$). Furthermore, we derive the basic reproductive number for the SEIRS framework, establishing a link between the cycle duration and $\lambda$, the reciprocal of the average latent period. Utilizing these findings, we calculate the optimal duration of quarantine and isolation measures. Additionally, we determine the critical vaccination threshold required to achieve herd immunity.

Word embeddings have become a cornerstone of natural language processing, with the context window size being a critical hyperparameter. While prior research has predominantly favored larger windows, this study investigates the impact of window size on sentiment analysis and question answering. We introduce a novel selection strategy that determines the optimal window size for specific tasks and datasets by comparing good, improved, and best configurations. Results indicate that a smaller window of 2 is often superior to the larger windows typically recommended.

We examine the maximal clique number in high-density random geometric graphs, where vertex degrees are on the order of $\log n$. We demonstrate that, with high probability, the largest clique number is bounded above by $k$ whenever the reciprocal of the degree gap, $\delta$, satisfies $1/\delta \geq (1-\epsilon)\log 4$. This result sharpens a previous finding by Alishahi and Panahi, who established the bound for degrees asymptotic to $n^\alpha$ with $\alpha \in (0,1)$. Our approach builds upon the method introduced by Alishahi and Navasi, who derived an upper bound for degrees scaling as $n^\alpha$ with $\alpha \in (0,1/2)$.

This paper introduces a Lagrangian formulation for stars composed of spinning particles, treating the system as a mixture of fluids. The resulting framework encompasses both the standard Fermi-liquid description and the broader case of anisotropic fluids. The study establishes the governing equations of motion, the thermodynamic relations, and the associated conservation laws. Furthermore, it examines the thermodynamic potentials and their corresponding conjugate fields. The authors demonstrate that the formalism can be extended to incorporate quantum effects, specifically the Landau-Lifshitz boundary term, and briefly considers the implications of these findings for neutron stars.

This study examines the Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) solution within a Palatini $f(R)$ framework, where the gravitational action is defined as $f(R) = R + 2\Lambda + \alpha R^2$ and $\alpha$ represents a small parameter. The analysis reveals that the solution is valid only when the Ricci scalar is negligible ($R \approx 0$). Consequently, the standard LBT metric remains a robust and reliable model for describing the universe's evolution, even under the influence of higher-order corrections in $f(R)$ gravity.

Quantum nonlocality, a cornerstone of quantum information theory, is typically examined through the lens of nonlocal games or Bell-type inequalities. In this work, we investigate $N$-partite nonlocality using a framework based on the probability distribution of measurement outcomes. We introduce a family of $N$-partite inequalities that breach the nonlocal bound; notably, the maximal violation of these inequalities remains unaffected by uniform local unitary operations, ensuring robustness against local noise. We demonstrate that the maximal violation of the $N$-partite inequality is achieved by a specific class of $N$-partite pure states, thereby establishing their entanglement. Furthermore, we derive an upper limit on the maximal violation for $N$-partite mixed states, which provides an entanglement criterion for such systems.

This study examines the task of forecasting a user's visual attention on brief temporal windows using only prior gaze data. We introduce a novel deep learning architecture that integrates both raw and processed gaze features to address this challenge. The proposed model is evaluated against a baseline that relies exclusively on raw gaze signals. Our findings indicate that leveraging processed features significantly enhances prediction accuracy compared to using raw data alone. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our approach outperforms baseline models across various window durations.

The research community has recently identified reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) as a transformative technology for wireless communication, enabling the dynamic adjustment of electromagnetic wave propagation. While RIS has primarily focused on reflective modes, emerging studies suggest that transmissive RIS (TRIS) can overcome the line-of-sight (LoS) limitations inherent in reflective systems, thereby establishing new possibilities for wireless connectivity. This paper introduces a novel transometric RIS (TRIS) designed to enhance 6G network connectivity. The study details the development of a 16-element TRIS prototype, the formulation of a transmission model, and the integration of this system into a wireless testbed. Experimental results validate the system's ability to create new connectivity links, even in LoS-deficient environments. Furthermore, the work evaluates the system's performance under varying transmission distances and frequencies, while also addressing key implementation challenges and outlining future research directions.

Offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) involves training a policy using a fixed dataset of state-action pairs without further rollouts. This work examines the Linear-Optimization Structure (LOS) within offline RL, a framework that enables the application of linear-programming-style algorithms to achieve optimal regret bounds. We investigate how LOS extends to non-parametric function approximation, a critical advancement for handling large or infinite state spaces. Specifically, we introduce a novel, general functional framework that demonstrates LOS efficacy across a wide spectrum of non-parametric models, including neural networks and graph-based methods. Our theoretical findings establish that LOS-based algorithms can reach an optimal regret rate of $\tilde{O}(dH\sqrt{dH/K_n})$ for any offline algorithm utilizing a general function estinator with this property, where $d$ represents the estimator's effective dimension and $K$ denotes the sample size. We substantiate the versatility of this framework by verifying that several contemporary non-parametric models possess the requisite structural properties. Furthermore, we validate the practical efficacy of LOS-based algorithms under non-parametric settings through empirical experiments.
In this work, we demonstrate the construction of an entire collection of homotopy types using only free groups.

This discovery stems from the detection of a broad, blueshifted broad emission line (BL) in the spectrum of the quasar, which exhibits a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 10,000 km/s.
